text: dsh-chrome-devtools 是一个面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Chrome 浏览器接入插件。它通过配置 bundle 挂载 browser-use 服务和 Chrome DevTools MCP provider，让 Harness 会话获得浏览器接入能力。插件默认在每个新会话启动独立 Chrome，也可配置为连接用户自行启动的 Chrome，并设置是否显示窗口及浏览器可执行文件路径。适合需要在 DSH 会话中接入 Chrome 的用户；默认配置无需额外 API 密钥，需安装 Chrome。

dsh-chrome-devtools connects Harness sessions to Chrome by mounting browser-use and Chrome DevTools MCP. It launches an isolated browser by default, or attaches to a user-started browser. Headless mode and the Chrome executable path are configurable. Chrome is required; no API key is configured.
想让 DSH 会话接入一个真实的 Chrome 浏览器。
能不能让每个新聊天都启动独立的浏览器？
我想把自己已经打开的 Chrome 连接给 Harness 使用。
如何让浏览器在没有桌面显示器的环境里以无头模式启动？
I want my Harness chat to connect to a Chrome browser.
Can each new DSH session get its own launched browser?
How can I attach a chat to a Chrome instance I started myself?
I need the browser provider to run headlessly on a server.
dsh-chrome-devtools 的功能「接入 Chrome provider」：bundle 挂载 browser-use 服务和 Chrome DevTools MCP provider，供 Harness 会话接入浏览器。
dsh-chrome-devtools 的功能「启动独立浏览器」：默认使用 launch 模式，为每个活动会话启动隔离的 Chrome，且默认显示浏览器窗口。
dsh-chrome-devtools 的功能「连接现有浏览器」：将模式配置为 attach 并提供 endpoint，可让 provider 连接用户自行启动的 Chrome。

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome DevTools：Give your DeepSeek Harness Agent a real Chrome browser to drive and inspect.

This plugin installs [Chrome DevTools MCP](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp)
as the Harness browser provider, so the Agent works a Chrome window you can
watch. It opens pages, reads them, clicks and types, takes screenshots, reads
console messages and network requests, runs scripts, records performance traces,
and runs Lighthouse audits.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome DevTools：Chrome belongs to the chat that opened it. Close the chat and its browser goes
with it, so one conversation can never drive another one's pages.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · What you can ask for：- *"Open example.com, screenshot it, and tell me the console errors."*
- *"Go to my app on localhost:3000, sign up with a test account, and tell me
  whether the confirmation step works."*
- *"Record a performance trace on localhost:3000 and explain the largest
  contentful paint."*
- *"Run a Lighthouse audit on localhost:3000 and tell me what fails
  accessibility."*
- *"Screenshot that page at 375 pixels wide so I can check the mobile layout."*
- *"Click the thing that is broken and tell me exactly what the network request
  returns."*

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Install：1. In the Harness, open **Plugins** in the left sidebar.
2. Press **Install**.
3. Paste this repository's address:

```
   https://github.com/DevTarlow/dsh-chrome-devtools
   ```

4. Install it, then refresh the page.
5. **Start a new chat.** The Agent connects a browser when a chat begins, so a
   chat that was already open when you installed keeps running without one.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Install：The install dialog accepts a GitHub address, a package name, or a local folder.
To pin the release this README describes, paste
`github:DevTarlow/dsh-chrome-devtools#v0.1.0` instead. If you would rather ask
your Agent, say: *"Install the bundle `github:DevTarlow/dsh-chrome-devtools`."*

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Install：You need Google Chrome (or Chrome for Testing) at its current stable version.
The plugin finds it by itself, so a normal installation needs no configuration.
You also need a desktop session, because the browser opens a real window.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Check it works：In a new chat, ask:

> Open example.com and tell me its title and any console errors.

A Chrome window opens, loads the page, and the Agent answers from what it read.
If you would rather not open a window, see `headless` under [Settings](#settings).

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Settings：The plugin's defaults are set in [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml). To change
one, put the same override in your own Harness profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — for
example `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` — then start a new chat.

```yaml
- id: browser-use-chrome-devtools
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp'
  config:
    mode: launch

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Settings：Any setting you leave out falls back to the plugin's own default rather than this
bundle's, so restate every value you still want whenever you edit that block.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Settings：| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `launch` | `launch` starts a fresh Chrome for each chat. Use `attach` to drive a browser you started yourself. |
| `headless` | `false` | `false` opens a window you can watch. Set `true` on a server or in CI, where there is no display. |
| `executablePath` | unset | Which Chrome to launch. Left unset, the plugin finds it. Set it for an unusual install, or for the wrapper in [Common questions](#common-questions). |
| `endpoint` | — | Required by `attach`: the debugging address of the browser you started, such as `http://127.0.0.1:9222`. |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | the client's own | How long one tool call may take, in milliseconds. |

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Drive your own browser instead：`launch` gives every chat a fresh profile, which means it starts logged out. To
keep the tabs, cookies and logins you already have, start Chrome yourself and
point the plugin at it.

```sh
google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="$HOME/.dsh-chrome"
```

```yaml
- id: browser-use-chrome-devtools
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp'
  config:
    mode: attach

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Drive your own browser instead：One chat holds that browser at a time. When the chat ends, the plugin disconnects
and leaves your browser running.

Start that browser before you open a chat. The plugin connects when a chat is
created, so a chat started while the browser is unreachable has no browser tools.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome extensions：The browser this plugin launches is a clean, isolated profile with extensions
disabled, so it cannot load or test an unpacked extension. To test one, attach
the plugin to a Chrome you start yourself, with the extension already loaded:

```yaml
- id: browser-use-chrome-devtools
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp'
  config:
    mode: attach

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome extensions：The plugin then drives the pages with its normal browser tools. It does not pass
Chrome DevTools MCP's `--category-extensions` flag, so the extension-specific
tools (`install_extension`, `reload_extension`, `list_extensions`,
`trigger_extension_action`) and `chrome-extension://` pages are not available
through the plugin. Use the `chrome-devtools` CLI from the same pinned
`chrome-devtools-mcp` release for those:

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome extensions：```sh
chrome-devtools start --browser-url http://127.0.0.1:9222 --categoryExtensions=true
chrome-devtools list_extensions
chrome-devtools install_extension /absolute/path/to/unpacked-extension
chrome-devtools reload_extension <extension-id>

Loading an extension over a browser URL needs Chrome 149 or newer. Stop the CLI
daemon with `chrome-devtools stop` when you are done.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Chrome extensions：Use a dedicated profile for that browser. The debugging port gives anything on
the machine full control of it, so keep it bound to localhost and stop the
browser when you finish testing.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Use your existing logged-in Chrome：Chrome 136+ does not allow `--remote-debugging-port` against the default profile,
but you can let the CLI attach to the Chrome you are already using. Enable
Chrome's remote debugging bridge (Chrome 144+):

1. Open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` in that Chrome.
2. Turn on **Enable remote debugging** and leave the browser running.
3. Click **Allow** when Chrome asks to allow the session.

The CLI finds that browser itself:

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Use your existing logged-in Chrome：```sh
chrome-devtools start --auto-connect --channel=stable --categoryExtensions=true
chrome-devtools list_extensions
```

For the plugin, read the browser's websocket endpoint and use it as the attach
endpoint:

```sh
PORT=$(head -1 ~/.config/google-chrome/DevToolsActivePort)
WSPATH=$(sed -n 2p ~/.config/google-chrome/DevToolsActivePort | tr -d '\r')
```

```yaml
- id: browser-use-chrome-devtools
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp'
  config:
    mode: attach

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Use your existing logged-in Chrome：The port and browser ID change when Chrome restarts or the toggle is turned off
and on; update the endpoint and start a new chat. While remote debugging is on,
the agent can read every tab, cookie, and login in that profile. Turn it off at
`chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` when you finish testing.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**The browser tools are missing.** Start a new chat. The plugin connects a
browser when a chat is created, so chats that were already open do not have one.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**Chrome exits immediately, or the Agent reports `No usable sandbox!`.** Chrome
cannot start with its own sandbox on your machine. This is common in containers
and WSL, on Ubuntu 23.10+ where AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces,
and wherever `/opt/google/chrome/chrome-sandbox` is not owned by `root` with mode
`4755`. Repairing that needs root. Otherwise launch Chrome through a wrapper that
adds `--no-sandbox` and point `executablePath` at it:

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：```sh
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /usr/bin/google-chrome --no-sandbox "$@"\n' > ~/chrome-no-sandbox
chmod +x ~/chrome-no-sandbox
```

```yaml
        executablePath: /home/you/chrome-no-sandbox
```

That runs untrusted page content without the operating system's sandbox. Fix the
sandbox if you can, and treat the wrapper as a last resort.

**`Missing X server to start the headful browser`.** Your machine has no display.
Set `headless: true`.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**The page shows a login wall, or the browser starts empty.** That is what a
fresh profile looks like. Use `attach` above to bring your own logged-in browser.

**A screenshot arrives as text instead of a picture.** Your model route has to
accept images, and your profile needs an attachment store, for the image to reach
the model.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**Saving a screenshot to a file is refused.** The browser tools may only write
under your operating system's temp directory — a path inside your project is
answered with `Access denied: path … is not within any of the configured
workspace roots`. Ask for the screenshot as an image instead; it reaches the model
without touching the filesystem.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**Installing was rejected for incompatible peers.** The browser packages this
plugin builds on are pre-stable and pin the Harness version exactly. Update the
two `dependencies` in [package.json](package.json) to the versions that match your
Harness release.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Common questions：**The console prints `Update available: 1.9.0 -> 1.10.1`.** That notice comes from
the Chrome DevTools MCP server this plugin mounts, not from the plugin itself, and
the version it offers is chosen by DeepSeek Harness. The `npm install` it suggests
does nothing here: the plugin starts its own pinned copy, so running that command
only adds a stray dependency wherever you ran it. Ignore the notice, or start the
Harness with `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS=1` to silence it.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Limits：- One browser plugin per Harness. Do not also install the Playwright or Stagehand
  browser providers.
- Chromium only. Firefox and WebKit are not offered.
- A launched browser belongs to one chat. Reloading or resuming a chat starts
  fresh browser state; the conversation does not restore cookies or pages.
- Cancelling a call cannot undo a navigation or click that already happened.
- Tool definitions come from the pinned `chrome-devtools-mcp` release, not from
  the Harness, so they carry no stability promise.
- Usage statistics are off. Performance tools otherwise behave as upstream
  documents them, including sending trace URLs to the Google CrUX API.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · Removing it：Open **Plugins**, find **dsh-chrome-devtools**, and uninstall it. Chats you start
afterwards have no browser tools. If you added a `cordis.patch.yml` override,
delete that block too.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · For developers：This repository is a configuration-only bundle: two files, no build step.

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml) | the two rows this bundle inserts and their defaults |
| [verify-live.mjs](verify-live.mjs) | a check that drives the MCP server without a Harness |

`verify-live.mjs` lists the tool catalog, opens a URL, reads the page title, and
writes a screenshot. Run it from a DeepSeek Harness source checkout:

dsh-chrome-devtools README · For developers：```sh
cd packages/experimental/browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp
export DSH_MCP_CLI=$(node --input-type=module -e "import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url'; console.log(fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve('chrome-devtools-mcp/build/src/bin/chrome-devtools-mcp.js')))")
cd ../../..
export DSH_MCP_SDK=$PWD/packages/mcp/mcp-client/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/client/dist

dsh-chrome-devtools README · For developers：Set `DSH_MCP_HEADLESS=true` only in a shell that cannot reach the X server; the
bundle itself opens a window. Set `DSH_MCP_EXECUTABLE` to test a particular Chrome
or a wrapper.

dsh-chrome-devtools README · For developers：The two `dependencies` in `package.json` are the whole reason this plugin works on
a released Harness: the browser packages are not part of a published `dsh`, so
they install with the bundle. A profile that installs this repository from a git
spec installs them. A profile that links this directory as a local bundle does
not, and the rows then resolve from whatever the Harness installation carries.
